rubric.correct: Every actually requested fact correct, resolved and summary-supported; equivalent complete meaning accepted; no material contradiction.
rubric.partial: Missing/unresolved requested fact with no material contradiction.
rubric.incorrect: Any material contradiction, including volunteered contextual claims.

global_constraints: No borrowing a fact from another question or reader.
Do not require ancillary source-only facts or contextual key facts excluded here.
Named board order may convey an order without listing every suit.
A clear operational equivalent passes without parroting key wording.
Semantic relation must be present: one user is not once total; paid use is not necessarily user pays; global three Visions is not personal draws; one unmatched site card is not all unmatched.
Free Chronicle together with affirmative Exile-winner permission may convey normal-offer waiver.
This file does not certify source audit or silently fix a fixed expected answer.

questions.question: Bandits rule more faceup sites than any player. Do they compete for the Oathkeeper or Vision goals or prevent a player from having the most sites among players?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No. Bandits act as a neutral defender for Campaign purposes and rule empty faceup sites, but they do not compete for victory goals. Compare the relevant players, not bandits, when resolving those goals.
questions.source_references: Playbook p32 Campaigns; Law Glossary Rule as corrected by errata; Law 2.11; Law 3.2

required_facts.expected_fact: No competition for title/Visions; compare relevant players, ignoring bandits for most-sites goals.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Bandits neutral Campaign defender and rule empty faceup sites.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Background facts/premise not additional requested victory eligibility criteria.

questions.question: At Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City, when and from where may a player take income? Can they take both one favor and one secret, use a remotely ruled site, or take from a bank if that site is empty?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: At the end of Wake, after the People’s Favor procedure, Exile win check and title flip, a player whose pawn is at the eligible site may take one favor or one secret from that site. It is one token total, not one of each; remote rule alone does not qualify, and an empty site supplies nothing rather than a substitute token from a bank.
questions.source_references: Law 4.1.1–4; Site Reference p2 Opportunity Sites; Law 9.3

required_facts.expected_fact: End Wake after banner/win/title steps; pawn at eligible site may take one favor OR one secret from that site.
One token total, not one each; remote rule insufficient; empty site gives nothing, no substitute bank token.

questions.question: The attacker loses a Campaign. The defender used a battle plan saying “If you're victorious,” and both players used plans saying “At end, discard [card name].” What resolves after the roll, in what order, and does losing let the attacker keep their end-discard plan?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Resolve the defeated attacker's losses first: kill half of the warbands remaining in their force, rounded down, keep the survivors on their board, then resolve any battle plans they used that say “If you're defeated.” Skip the attacker's target-taking step because the attacker lost. In Step 8, resolve the victorious defender's “If you're victorious” battle plans. Then discard the applicable “At end, discard [card name]” plans used by either player. The defeated attacker still discards such a plan; the end-discard instruction does not require its user to have won. Apply the text of each effect, including any optional parts.
questions.source_references: Law 5.5.6 Resolve Defeat, printed p7; Law 5.5.7 Resolve Attacker's Victory, printed p7; Law 5.5.8 Resolve Battle Plans, printed p7; Law 7.1.3 Use (resolve as much as possible except may parts), printed p9

required_facts.expected_fact: Kill half defeated attacker’s remaining force rounded down, keep survivors board, resolve defeated effects.
Skip attacker target-taking; resolve victorious defender plans.
Then discard applicable end-discard plans used by either player; losing does not preserve attacker’s plan.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Apply exact effect text/optional may portions.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: General resolution hierarchy is context; actual effects’ text is not provided and no new hypothetical content is required.

questions.question: A battle plan you rule has a gradient power box and a ± attack-die symbol. Must an attacker add the die and a defender remove it, or may either user choose either sign? Does ± also let you change defense dice?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Either the attacker or defender may use a gradient battle plan and choose to add or remove the attack die shown. The plus/minus symbol means add or remove the type of die shown; it does not switch an attack-die effect into a defense-die effect, and the user’s role does not choose the sign. Normal battle-plan access, payment and once-per-Campaign rules still apply.
questions.source_references: Law 7.5.4 Iconography, printed p9: battle plans with a +/– symbol can add or remove the type of die shown.; Law 7.5 introductory paragraph, printed p9: gradient boxes allow attacker or defender.; Law 7.5.1–3, printed p9: rule/access, use timing, payment and use limit.; Card Reference p1 Common Icons: Add or remove symbol.

required_facts.expected_fact: Either attacker/defender may use gradient plan and choose plus or minus; role does not select sign.
Only shown attack die is added/removed; ± does not convert effect to defense die.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question premises ruled plan and asks role/sign/type; full battle-plan procedure is ancillary, not an added requirement.

questions.question: You have a faceup card effect beginning “Wake:” whose text contains no “may”. May you choose to skip it because it would be inconvenient, just as you can decline a “Rest:” power? Is taking Opportunity-site income at Wake compulsory too?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No. Wake powers happen during your Wake Phase, once each; you do not have a general option to skip such a Wake effect. Resolve as much of its effect as possible, respecting its conditions and other restrictions, except any parts that explicitly say “may”. Rest powers are optional and may be used once each at the end of Rest. Taking one favor or secret at Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City is explicitly optional, so you may decline that income.
questions.source_references: Law7.3.1 Wake, printed p9: Wake powers happen once each during Wake; the reminder distinguishes mandatory powers from optional taking of site favor/secrets.; Law7.3.4 Rest and Law4.3.5, printed pp9,5: Rest powers may be used once each at end of Rest.; Law7.1.3 Use, printed p9: must resolve as much as possible except parts saying may.; Law4.1.4 Use Site Power, printed p5; Site Reference p2 Opportunity Sites: may take one favor or secret.

required_facts.expected_fact: No general option to skip; Wake powers once in Wake, resolve as much as possible subject to conditions/restrictions and explicit may parts.
Rest powers optional once each at end Rest.
Taking one favor/secret at named eligible sites is expressly optional, may decline.

questions.question: A Red Exile’s pawn is at a faceup site garrisoned by purple warbands, while red warbands occupy a different faceup site without their pawn. Which site and its denizen cards does Red rule? Does moving the pawn by itself change rule, and can red and purple site warbands coexist to share rule of one site?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Red rules the faceup site containing their red warbands and the cards at that site, even though their pawn is elsewhere. Red does not rule the purple-garrisoned site merely because their pawn is there. A player also rules their own advisers. Moving a pawn by itself does not move the site warbands or change this basis of rule. A site can hold warbands of only one color at a time; different colors do not share a site by coexisting there. Imperial players share rule of purple-garrisoned sites under the Empire exception, rather than by placing different colors together.
questions.source_references: Law 10, Rule, corrected by errata to faceup sites; Law 6.6.3 Imperial Players; Playbook p8, Ruling Sites on the Map; Playbook p18: pawns do not matter for rule

required_facts.expected_fact: Red rules red-garrisoned faceup site and its cards despite pawn elsewhere; not purple site merely from pawn presence.
Pawn alone does not move garrisons or change rule basis.
Only one warband color per site; red/purple cannot coexist to share rule.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question names sites and their denizen cards, not adviser ownership; this is purely contextual key material.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Imperial players share purple-garrisoned sites through Empire exception.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Explains a different sharing situation; Red is specified Exile and question asks coexistence of colors, so no independent Imperial-rule recital required.

questions.question: A power tells you to reveal a facedown card, without telling you to play it. Who sees its front? Is this the same instruction as peeking, and does revealing alone award favor for site play or trigger a When Played power?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Reveal means show the card’s front to everyone. Peek means the prompted player looks at its front. Revealing alone is not an instruction to Play: it does not itself put a card at a site, in advisers, or in a personal bank. Therefore the reveal alone does not grant the favor for playing to a site or trigger a When Played power. If the effect separately instructs you to play the card, follow that instruction and the ordinary play restrictions and triggers.
questions.source_references: Law 10, Reveal, Peek, Play; Law 9.1 literal interpretation; Law 5.1.4.I gain for playing to site; Law 7.3.3 When Played

required_facts.expected_fact: Reveal shows front to everyone; Peek lets prompted player look.
Reveal alone is not Play and gives neither site-play favor nor When Played trigger.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Enumerate all Play destinations and hypothetical separate Play instruction.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Destination list/alternate effect is explanatory context; asked distinction and trigger consequences are complete without it.

questions.question: While resolving a power, an instruction says to do something “after” a specified event. May you postpone that instruction until after an intervening step of the same action? What exact timing does “after” prescribe?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No. After means immediately following: nothing happens between the specified event and the prompted instruction. It does not provide a discretionary later window within the action. Follow any explicit text governing the actual effect; this definition does not invent a priority rule for simultaneous effects.

required_facts.expected_fact: No; immediately following, nothing between event and instruction, no discretionary later action window.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Actual effect text and simultaneous-effect priority disclaimer.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question asks definition/timing of after; it does not ask priority between simultaneous effects or unspecified effect text.

questions.question: Unless an effect specifies different locations, where do favor/secrets, an adviser card, and a relic move when you Take them? How does Give reverse the direction? If a power simply tells you to Burn a favor or secret, can you choose a token on a banner or card instead of your board, and where does it go?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Take moves the prompted favor or secrets from the prompted player’s board to your board, a card from their advisers to your advisers, or a relic from their personal bank—or the prompted site or draw source—to your personal bank. Give is the reverse direction of Take. Burn normally moves the prompted favor or secret from your own board to the shared bank; another location is used only if the effect prompts it. A plain Burn instruction does not let you substitute a token from a banner or card. Follow the actual prompt and applicable placement/restriction rules.
questions.source_references: Law 10, Take, Give, Burn; Law 9.1 literal interpretation

required_facts.expected_fact: Favor/secrets prompted player board→own board; adviser card their advisers→own advisers.
Relic their personal bank (or explicitly prompted site/source)→own personal bank.
Reverse Take direction.
Own-board favor/secret→shared bank; cannot substitute banner/card token absent prompted different location.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Not independently asked by default transfer-location question; no contradictory permission is allowed.

questions.question: A power permits an Exchange with a prompted player, without adding a must instruction or a binding agreement. What permission does Exchange give each player? Does the word alone require both players to transfer equal amounts in a simultaneous swap?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Exchange means you may Give to the prompted player and vice versa: each player has the stated permission to Give to the other. The word by itself does not impose a compulsory, equal-amount, simultaneous exchange. The actual power still controls which pieces and amounts are permitted, and any explicit binding promise or other instruction must be followed. Swap is a different instruction that moves the two prompted pieces to each other’s locations.
questions.source_references: Law 10, Exchange, Give, Take, Swap; Law 9.1 literal interpretation; Law 7.6.3 and 9.6 for the separate binding-promise rule

required_facts.expected_fact: Each may Give to prompted other player, in both directions, within actual power’s permitted pieces/amounts.
Word alone imposes none of compulsory, equal amounts, or simultaneous transfer.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Explicit binding promises/other must instructions still followed.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question expressly excludes them; separate binding mechanism is background.
Contrasts a different keyword; answer need not define Swap to deny that Exchange requires one.

questions.question: The previous game was packed without rebuilding the world deck. During later-game setup, may you seed the regional discards and deal starting advisers from that unrebuilt stack, then rebuild the deck afterward? At exactly what point must the deferred rebuild happen?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No. If the world deck was not rebuilt during the last Chronicle, perform the rebuild in the Law setup box before setup step19. Reconstruct the top12 cards from ten denizens plus two random Visions, the next18 from fifteen denizens plus the other three Visions, with remaining denizens below. Only then take the three total bottom cards to seed the three discard piles in step19, followed by each player drawing three bottom cards in step20. Do not seed or deal from the unrebuilt stack and rebuild afterward.
questions.source_references: Law printed p3 setup box before step19; Law1.19–20; Law8.8

required_facts.expected_fact: If the previous Chronicle did not rebuild the world deck, rebuild before regional discard seeding and before starting-adviser bottom draws; do not perform those draws from the unrebuilt stack and rebuild afterward.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Repeated10+2/15+3/rest rebuild recipe and exact numbered Law step labels
contextual_exclusions.rationale: The question asks trigger and order, already established recipe has zero novelty credit. A clear operational before-any-seeding/dealing answer suffices without Law step numbers.
contextual_exclusions.contradiction_policy: Absence not penalized; materially false volunteered recipe/order still incorrect.

questions.semantic_notes: Before seeding regional discards and dealing starting advisers is the operational equivalent of before Law step19. Do not demand the summary's step numbers match the original Law numbering.

questions.question: During first-game packet setup, how are the Chancellor and other players seated? In later-game setup, must the previous winner become Chancellor, and how are seats assigned before the other players choose boards?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: For the first game, choose one player as Chancellor and seat them on the short edge near the Cradle; seat Red, Blue and Yellow in that clockwise order from the Chancellor. In later-game setup, choose the Chancellor in any way: the previous winner is recommended, not required. Seat the Chancellor next to the Cradle and seat the other players randomly. Non-Chancellors then choose among the boards on their Chronicled sides in that turn order.
questions.source_references: Law printed p2 Setup1.7; Law1.9 for the already-tested subsequent board choice; Playbook printed p6 setup8; printed p7 setup10

required_facts.expected_fact: The Chancellor sits by the Cradle in both first-game and later-game setup (first game at the short edge).
First packet setup seats Red, then Blue, then Yellow clockwise from the Chancellor.
Later setup chooses the Chancellor by any method; previous winner is recommended, not required.
Later setup seats the other players randomly before non-Chancellors make their saved-board choices in the resulting turn order.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Full board-eligibility rules beyond seating-before-choice order

questions.question: Which goal reference does the first-game packet setup use, and what are its Oathkeeper and Successor goals? Does that setup allow choosing any of the four Oaths?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: The first-game packet setup uses the Oathkeeper of Supremacy goal reference. Its Oathkeeper goal is to rule the most sites; its Successor goal is to hold more relics and banners in total than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. The Chancellor begins with the Oathkeeper title. The printed first-game setup specifies Supremacy rather than offering a free choice among the four Oaths; later games use the goal selected in the preceding Chronicle.
questions.source_references: Playbook printed p6 setup6: shared pieces include the Oathkeeper of Supremacy goal reference; Playbook printed p8 The Chancellor: in your first game, Chancellor begins as Oathkeeper of Supremacy; Playbook printed p26 Winning as a Citizen; Law3.3.1 for already-tested Successor definition; Law1.3 and8.1 for already-tested later Chronicled reference

required_facts.expected_fact: First packet setup specifically uses Oathkeeper of Supremacy; it does not allow a free choice of any Oath.
Supremacy Oathkeeper goal is to rule the most sites.
Supremacy Successor goal is more total relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Chancellor starting title and later Chronicle goal-selection procedure

evidence: Citizen succession is a separate test

questions.question: During the Chronicle’s edifice-ruining step, an applicable power has already kept a site that the winner does not rule. It has no intact edifice to flip. Does that step discard its denizens just because the site is retained and unruled? What actually triggers that step’s denizen discard?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No. Law8.3.3 discards denizens only at retained sites where an intact edifice actually flipped to ruin in that step. The winner not ruling a site, or a power retaining it, does not itself trigger that discard. Other retained sites keep their denizens unless another applicable instruction discards them; the earlier disposal of cards on discarded sites is a separate operation.
questions.source_references: Law8.3.2–3,9.1; Playbookp4 embedded Chronicle aid, Forest Temple retention power (power effect supplied, no card recall required)

required_facts.expected_fact: No denizen discard through this ruining step in the given case: it occurs only at sites where an intact edifice actually flipped to ruin, not merely because a site is retained and unruled.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Named Forest Temple recall, full site-disposal destinations, other possible power instructions and subsequent map packing
contextual_exclusions.rationale: The question supplies retention and asks the actual-flip guard for this one step.
contextual_exclusions.contradiction_policy: Omission not penalized; any volunteered materially false universal claim still incorrect.

questions.semantic_notes: The site is already retained; apply the present ruining-step condition. Do not infer a discard from lack of winner rule alone. Equivalent complete meaning accepted.
